 1.
Despite the notice to the informant-prosecutrix, none appears for the informant.

2. The petitioner is an accused in connection with Koraput Sadar P.S. Case No.89 of 2024 corresponding to G.R. Case No.564 of 2024 for the offences punishable under Sections 366/ 376(2)
(n)/ 376(3) of the IPC read with Section 4(2)/6 of the POCSO Act pending in the Court of the learned Additional Sessions Judge-cum-Special Court under POCSO Act, Jeypore.
The petitioner had approached the learned P.O., Special Court under POCSO Act, Jeypore in G.R. Case No.564 of 2024 praying for grant of bail.
The learned Court below vide its order dated 15.05.2024 rejected the bail application of the petitioner.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. praying for enlargement on bail.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner, on instruction from the petitioner, submits that, except the present bail application, no other bail application of the petitioner is pending in any other Court relating to the aforesaid F.I.R.
4.
The prosecution case as per the F.I.R. is that, on 02.05.2024, the complainant reported at Bidanasi P.S. alleging that, the victim, who was aged 16 years, was pregnant.
When she enquired about the same she came to know that, the present petitioner was having sexual relationship with her and responsible for the criminal act.

Hence the F.I.R.

1 5.
In the present case, the victim has been examined by the trial Court as P.W.1.
She, in her statement, has taken a completely different stand.

The statement in paragraph-3 of her examination-in-chief reads as under:
"3. My brother-in-law (A1) had come to our village and he told to convene a village meeting.
A1 told me as the said Sanjay would not take me with him, I should stay in his house till delivery of my child out of my pregnancy.
He further told me that he would take care of my child after delivery.
I had made phone call to the said Sanjay and my brother-in-law (A1) scolded him for his relationship with me causing my pregnancy.

However, the Anganwadi didi had initiated this case against my brother-in-law (A1) for no fault on his part."
6.
The petitioner is the accused No.1(A1), who is the brother-in-law of the victim.

In the statement,
the victim has fully exonerated the petitioner.
Even the DNA test report has not supported the prosecution case.

The petitioner has been in custody since 03.05.2024.
7.

In view of the testimony of the victim girl and the medical evidence including the DNA test and the fact that the petitioner has been in custody since 03.05.2024, I am inclined to admit the petitioner on bail.

In the event the petitioner is found wanting for violation of any of the bail conditions imposed by this Court or the trial Court even on a single occasion, the prosecution is at liberty to move appropriate application before the Court below for cancellation of the concession of bail granted by this Court.
If such application is filed, the trial Court should decide the application on its own merit.
9. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
(S.S. Mishra) Judge Subhasis Location: High Court of Orissa, Cuttack.
